# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — empty seed: code payment-normalization/enriched errors + a procedural execution contract in the policy
- Changes I made:
  - tools.py `_coerce_payment_methods` + used in `book_reservation` (cluster: payment arg-filling, tasks 8/12) — maps `id`→`payment_id`, drops stray `type`/`source`, actionable error on missing `payment_id`/`amount`.
  - tools.py `book_reservation` enriched errors (cluster: payment-doesn't-add-up, 8/12/25) — names exact total, notes bag/insurance fees included, points to calculate; payment-not-found lists available ids; low-balance names balance.
  - tools.py `update_reservation_passengers` docstring worked example + enriched count-mismatch error (cluster: rename mis-count, 17/22).
  - tools.py literal per-param examples on `book_reservation` + `update_reservation_flights` (payment/flight shapes, cabin enum, cabin-only-change keeps existing segments).
  - policy.md +"How to actually execute a change" (cluster: narrated_without_action, 17/22/40) — after "yes", the very next step MUST be the write call; finish ALL writes; worked example.
  - policy.md +"Reusing a past or existing reservation" (8) — read get_reservation_details before replicating; don't guess from a fresh search.
  - policy.md +"Communicating the result" (11) — must state exact charge/refund + 5–7 day timeline + new flight details.
- Expected effect + why safe: code guards fire ONLY on malformed/mismatch inputs (verified identity on task 23's correct calls); update_* tools are not used by passing 19/23. Prompt additions are additive procedure/knowledge that MATCH passing behavior (19/23 already act after "yes" and look up reservations) — no refusal rule loosened, no act-where-refuse flip introduced.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — first iteration, empty seed, LEDGER/RUNMAP/rejected all empty.
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: narrated_without_action is the biggest (17/22/40) and is only addressable via prompt here (the agent emits NO tool call, so no code can force it). If the prompt contract doesn't land, next lever to try: a single composite `apply_reservation_changes(reservation_id, {passengers?, baggages?, cabin?})` that collapses the 2–3 required writes into ONE call (fewer act-turns for a weak model), and REMOVE the granular update_* primitives so the one call is the only path — but weigh generalization risk to held-out granular tasks.
- Plateau signal: n/a (iteration 1).
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, re-diagnose 37/25/12 with gold DB states (need the expected final state, not just the action-trace clue) to find the true DB mismatch; if rejected, check RESULT `broke={}` to see whether a prompt addition changed a passing trajectory and trim it.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.500 Δ=+0.300 · fixed={11, 12, 17, 25, 8} · broke={19, 23} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).

# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## Payment argument shape (book_reservation)
- What worked (pending RESULT confirmation, cand_0001): the mid model repeatedly sent `payment_methods=[{'id':..,'type':..}]` or added a stray `type` key → opaque pydantic traceback. An in-body `_coerce_payment_methods` normalizer (id→payment_id, drop type/source) makes these calls succeed and is identity on well-formed calls (verified on passing task 23).
- What didn't: n/a yet.
- Promising but not tried: normalizing the `flights` dicts the same way (they currently tolerate extra keys, so not yet needed).

## narrated_without_action is the dominant, non-code cluster
- Confirmed by traces (not yet by RESULT): tasks 17/22/40 gather info, present a plan, get "yes", then emit ZERO write calls and the episode ends. No tool-code edit can fix this (nothing to guard — the model calls nothing). Only levers: a crisp procedural prompt contract ("after yes, the next step IS the write call") and/or collapsing multiple required writes into one composite so fewer act-turns are needed.

## Verification harness for this suite
- The tau2 venv `/vol/home/skillberry/.cache/capevolve-ci/venv-skillberry-tau2/bin/python` loads the real airline DB and runs candidate tool bodies. Always use it to prove a guard FIRES on the failing-trace args and is a NO-OP on 1–2 passing-task args before shipping.

# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (run so far)
- Strategy tried: empty-seed first candidate. Mixed levers — in-body payment normalization + enriched errors (code) for arg-filling/recovery clusters, and additive procedural prompt sections for the behavioral/knowledge clusters. Verified every code edit by executing the tool body on exact trace args in the tau2 venv and confirming no fire on passing task 23. (Val result pending framework RESULT.)
- Key process win: a real tau2 venv exists at `/vol/home/skillberry/.cache/capevolve-ci/venv-skillberry-tau2/bin/python` and can load `FlightDB.load(AIRLINE_DB_PATH)` + instantiate the candidate tools — use it every iteration to VERIFY guards fire on failing args and are identity on passing args before shipping.
- Plateau/stall: n/a (iter 1). Note the dominant cluster (narrated_without_action, 3 hard zeros) is NOT code-fixable (agent emits no call) — it is the ceiling on how much pure-code work can move this suite. Prompt quality is the main lever for it.
- Diagnostic gap: the trajectory feedback gives the agent's write args but NOT the gold expected DB state, so tasks like 37 (write looked correct, still 0) can't be root-caused from the trace alone. Next iteration, pull the gold/expected final DB (see FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS) to crack 37/25/12.
- What to try next: if this is rejected on a passing-task regression, the suspect is a prompt addition changing 19/23's trajectory — bisect by shipping code-only first.

# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## cand_0001
- The per-task feedback gives the agent's OWN write args and "was never called" flags, but NOT the gold expected final DB state. For DB-scored tasks where the agent's write looks correct yet still scores 0 (e.g. task 37: correct flights/prices/refusal, still 0.000), the optimizer cannot root-cause the mismatch and is forced to either guess or skip. Please surface, per failing task, a diff of {agent final DB write(s)} vs {gold expected DB write(s)} (or at least the gold write args) — that single addition would convert several "un-diagnosable" clusters into fixable ones.
- The "8 ALWAYS-failing" summary embedded in INSTRUCTIONS truncates the action-trace detail mid-argument (e.g. "update_reservation_fli"), which is misleading; the full traces in ./trajectories/ are needed anyway. Either drop the truncated clue or make it a clean one-liner.
- A note in INSTRUCTIONS pointing to the local tau2 venv (it exists at .cache/capevolve-ci/venv-skillberry-tau2) as the sanctioned way to VERIFY tool-body guards would save every iteration the discovery step.

# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Empty seed → this is the first candidate. Reader = `aws/gpt-oss-120b` (mid tier), so I
pushed on code enforcement + literal, example-bearing docs, and made the prompt an
explicit procedure with a worked example.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | narrated_without_action | 17, 22, 40 | agent presents plan, user says "yes", agent emits NO write tool call (treats "yes" as completion) | BEHAVIORAL (no call emitted → cannot be code-forced) | prompt execution contract + worked example; reduce arg friction via docs |
| 2 | payment arg-filling errors | 8, 12 | payment_methods sent as `{'id':..,'type':..}` / with stray `type` key → opaque pydantic error, wasted turns | KNOWLEDGE + recoverable-error | in-body normalization guard in book_reservation + literal payment example in docs |
| 3 | "payment doesn't add up" strands/misleads | 8, 12, 25 | agent guesses the total; bare error doesn't say the total includes bag/insurance fees | recoverable-error | enriched actionable error text (+ point to calculate) |
| 4 | reference to past/existing flight not looked up | 8 | agent guessed a fresh-search flight instead of reading the referenced reservation | KNOWLEDGE | prompt rule: read get_reservation_details before replicating |
| 5 | rename mis-counted passengers | 17, 22 | agent thought replacing 1 of 2 passengers → 1 passenger (forbidden count change) | KNOWLEDGE | passenger tool docstring worked example + enriched count-mismatch error |
| 6 | missing required communication | 11 | write was correct but agent never told user the computed refund amount/timeline | KNOWLEDGE | prompt "communicate the result" contract |
| — (skipped) | 37, 25 (DB judgment), 12 (workaround) | see "Deliberately skipped" | — | — | — |

## Changes made this iteration
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | in-body normalization (lever 1) | tools.py `_coerce_payment_methods` + `book_reservation` | maps `id`→`payment_id`, drops stray `type`/`source`, raises short error if `payment_id`/`amount` missing. Fires only on a malformed dict; well-formed dicts pass through unchanged | yes — 23's correct dicts are identity |
| 3 | enriched error (lever 8) | tools.py `book_reservation` | "does not add up" now names the exact total, says it already includes bag/insurance fees, points to calculate; payment-not-found lists available ids; low-balance names balance | yes — only fires on the error path; 23 books cleanly |
| 5 | doc + enriched error | tools.py `update_reservation_passengers` | docstring worked example (Liam Lee→Omar Rossi keeps TWO entries) + count-mismatch error states current count and that count can't change | yes — passing tasks don't call it |
| 1,5 | schema/param docs | tools.py `book_reservation`, `update_reservation_flights` | literal per-param examples: payment `{"payment_id","amount"}`, flights `{"flight_number","date"}`, cabin enum, cabin-only-change keeps existing segments | doc-only |
| 1 | prompt procedure (additive) | policy.md "How to actually execute a change" | after user confirms, the VERY NEXT step MUST be the write call; multi-write requests must finish all writes; worked example | additive; matches 19/23 (they act after yes) |
| 4 | prompt rule (additive) | policy.md "Reusing a past or existing reservation" | read the referenced reservation before replicating; don't guess from a fresh search | additive; 23 already does this |
| 6 | prompt contract (additive) | policy.md "Communicating the result" | must state exact charge/refund + 5–7 day timeline + new flight details after any change | additive; communication-only, no DB change |

## Verify-the-fix (ran tool bodies on exact trace args via the tau2 venv)
- Task 8 `{'id':'certificate_8045380','type':'certificate','amount':114}` → normalized → books OK (price 114). Previously a pydantic error.
- Task 8 amount 500 vs total 114 → enriched error: "…total is 114, but …sum to 500. Adjust …to EXACTLY 114 …".
- Task 12 `{'type':'credit_card','payment_id':'credit_card_4938634','amount':849}` → stray `type` dropped → books OK (total 849).
- Task 17/22 `update_reservation_passengers('UM3OG5', [2 passengers])` → OK; passing 1 passenger → enriched "…has 2 passenger(s) but you passed 1…".
- SAFE: Task 23 (passing) correct 4-method book_reservation → still books, no regression. update_reservation_* untouched for 19/23 (they use cancel/book only).
- Import + `get_tools()` returns all 14 agent tools → registration intact; `py_compile` clean.

## Process & features used
- Serial (single agent). Used the tau2 venv at
  `/vol/home/skillberry/.cache/capevolve-ci/venv-skillberry-tau2/bin/python` to load the
  real FlightDB and execute tool bodies on exact trace args (VERIFIED + blast-radius).
- Prior iterations: none (first iteration; RUNMAP/LEDGER empty). rejected.jsonl empty.

## Good things to PRESERVE
- The payment normalization + enriched errors (bounded, verified) — keep.
- Do NOT loosen any refusal rule (basic-economy no-modify, cancellation eligibility,
  one-cert-per-reservation) — 19/23 and the correct refusals in 8/37 depend on them.
- Do NOT remove update_reservation_flights/passengers/baggages primitives.

## Deliberately skipped
- 37: agent's upgrade actually used the correct flights/prices and correctly refused the
  ineligible IFOYYZ cancellation; the DB mismatch cause isn't identifiable from the trace
  (likely card choice / gold nuance). No safe, general, verifiable edit → skipped rather
  than guess.
- 25/12 DB judgment (proceeding when the real total exceeded the user's stated figure /
  policy-workaround booking): needs a judgment call I can't encode generally without
  regressing legitimate multi-payment bookings (23). Partly nudged by the calculate/
  communicate prompt rules; not claimed as a hard fix.
- No composite `update_reservation_cabin` tool: verified it would reproduce the SAME
  graded write the agent already made on 37/11, so it changes no graded outcome → would
  be quota-filling. Dropped per the REAL test.
